findings.message: `storeGitHubApp` writes its own version of `keptExpiry` (apps/web/lib/admin/secrets.ts:39), but the two differ. When the current expiry has already passed, this copy quietly sets `expiresAt = null`, so the replaced credential never expires and never shows as Expiring again. That is the exact defect 052 fixed in rotate_secret. Fix: if the stored expiry is in the past, refuse the replace, or ask for a new expiry the way `keptExpiry` does. Don't drop it. Better still, reuse one shared rule. Add a test with a past expiry, a future expiry and no expiry.
findings.scenario: github-oauth expires 2026-11-01. On 2026-11-16 an Admin runs set_github_app. The new version is stored with expires_at null and never comes up as Expiring again.

findings.message: "Does the workspace have the GitHub app" is now decided by two different rules. `configured` (githubAppStatus, myGitAccounts, the chat suggestions, the Integrations chip, the Overview nudge) uses `hasSecret`, which leaves out expired credentials and expired versions. `hasGitHubApp`, `storeGitHubApp` and `rotatedAt` in read.ts:29 use `listCredentials` with `status !== 'revoked'`, which counts expired ones. So the screen and the card can contradict each other. Fix: use one predicate everywhere.
findings.scenario: github-oauth has expired. Integrations shows "Not configured" and chat suggests "Set up the GitHub app", but the card that opens is titled "Replace the GitHub app" and says the old secret works 72 more hours. Then the past expiry is dropped, as in the finding above.

findings.message: The `<client id>:<client secret>` format is checked in three places, and the checks disagree. (1) `checked` in secrets.ts refuses a second colon but takes any id or secret otherwise. (2) `app()` in server/app.ts:21 accepts a second colon (it splits at the first one). (3) `checkClientId`/`checkClientSecret` refuse spaces, `<>` and secrets shorter than 20 characters. Outside chat (MCP, where `propose` never runs), put_secret still stores github-oauth values that set_github_app would refuse. Fix: keep one parse/validate for the github-oauth value in the module and call it from every writer. Or make put_secret and rotate_secret refuse github-oauth outright at run, which is what their error message already tells the caller to do.
findings.scenario: An MCP client calls put_secret {connector:'github-oauth'} with 'my id:short'. It is stored. set_github_app with the same id and secret is refused with "the Client ID ... without spaces".

findings.message: The NO_KEY_SERVICE sentence is copied as a literal here and also defined in modules/git-accounts/words.ts:7. The mapping from SecretsUnavailableError to that refusal is written twice as well (here in `stored`, and `REFUSALS` in server/app.ts). If anyone edits one, the two will drift.

`callbackUrl` swallows every error from `redirectUri()` with an empty catch and returns null. In production without AMAX_BASE_URL, the status and the Integrations page drop the callback line without saying why. Either return the reason (for example `callbackUrl: null, callbackProblem: <message>`) or catch only that one ToolError.
findings.scenario: Production with AMAX_BASE_URL unset: Integrations shows "Configured" and no callback URL, with no hint about what is missing.

findings.message: `navigator.clipboard` is undefined outside a secure context. In that case `writeText` throws synchronously, before the `.then` failure handler is attached, so the "Couldn't copy" status never shows. Guard with `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` and fall back to the failure message.
findings.scenario: amax served over plain http at an internal k3s address: clicking Copy throws a TypeError and nothing is announced.

findings.message: The page is gated on `mcp:client:read` but now calls the `get_github_app_status` tool, which needs `git-accounts:read`, through the registry and with `source: "chat"`. A viewer with the first permission and not the second gets a page error instead of the card. A page render is also recorded as a chat call. Check the permission before calling, or degrade the card, and use the page's own source.
findings.scenario: A role holding mcp:client:read without git-accounts:read opens /settings/integrations and the render throws.

findings.message: `since: new Date().toISOString()` resets the nudge's waiting time on every load. It always reads as waiting 0h and, because the table shows the oldest first, it sorts last and can fall past the first six rows (SHOWN = 6). Use a stable time instead, such as when the app was set up or when the person joined.
findings.scenario: A person with 6 or more waiting decisions never sees the Connect GitHub nudge.

findings.message: `as unknown as McpToolDef` skips the type checks that the other tools get from `tool({...})`. A wrong `run`, `card` or `propose` signature would compile without error. Define it with `tool()` the way the tools in mcp.ts are.

The snooze is stored in localStorage under one key for the whole browser, not per person, so on a shared browser one person's 'Not now' hides the nudge from everyone. The first render also shows a snoozed nudge until the effect runs, so it flashes. Fix: key the stored map by the viewer's id.
findings.scenario: Kasun clicks Not now, then Nimal signs in on the same browser → Nimal never sees the Connect GitHub nudge for 30 days.
